task.title: Design typed provider outcomes and a versioned multi-provider session contract
task.description: Diagnose and design the Pi-core boundary that currently persists provider failures as semantically empty assistant messages. Define a typed non-conversational provider-outcome/session entry, migration and UI/event semantics, plus explicit additive-metadata evolution and conformance rules for session history consumed across providers. This task is investigation/design only on pg/ext/tool-span-coherence-tasks; any production implementation must be proposed for a fresh pg/core/* branch from main after upstream-parity review.

readBudget.guidance: Read the canonical message type, one verified producer, generic Pi message stream, SessionManager/context boundary, session-format docs, and overflow/compaction consumers. Expand to additional providers only for a bounded comparison matrix.

acceptanceCriteria: Inventory every layer that creates, persists, renders, retries, compacts, exports, or sends stopReason:error/aborted assistant messages with empty content; distinguish provider stream state from durable conversational history.

Define a typed provider-outcome entry/event that preserves human-visible error/retry/usage diagnostics while remaining outside provider-visible conversation history unless explicit visible assistant content exists.

Specify SessionEntry schema/version migration, branch/tree/context behavior, JSON/RPC/events, extension message hooks, UI rendering, resume/fork/compaction, and backward compatibility for existing empty error assistant records.

Define versioned multi-provider interchange evolution rules: semantic block/role/tool/chronology changes are versioned and fail closed; additive bounded numeric usage/cost metadata is non-semantic and forward-compatible; unknown executable/content-bearing shapes remain conservative.
Specify conformance fixtures that run each installed provider's error/abort output through persistence, buildSessionContext, model switch, compaction, and export without live paid-provider calls.

Assess whether the change is upstream-general and identify the exact pg/core branch, package ownership, implementation slices, review requirements, and migration risk. Do not claim an upstream fix before parity evidence.

Produce packages/coding-agent/docs/provider-outcome-session-contract.md with alternatives, rejected designs, staged rollout, compatibility boundary for extensions such as Claude Bridge, and a manager-ready implementation task split.
No production source/test/session mutation occurs in T004; only the design artifact and task bookkeeping may change.
